name: Making agents robust and safe in real scenarios
gist: Building agents that don't break when conditions change, can recover from adversarial situations, and avoid catastrophic failures even when faced with surprising or hostile inputs.
explain: A robot learned to reach a target in a lab, but in the real factory, the lighting is different and the gripper gets worn. An autonomous vehicle was trained on sunny roads but encounters rain. An AI trading system was trained on historical patterns that don't repeat. Adversarial settings are even worse: someone might actively try to trick the system. The problem is that when the real world differs from training, does the agent still work, or does it fail catastrophically?

Testing reliability is hard because you can't predict every difference between training and reality. Researchers test by intentionally distorting inputs — changing images, adding noise, warping physics — and checking if the agent still performs, which tells them which sources of variation break the system. But you also have to know which distortions matter most to fix first. A robot might handle camera angle changes (rotation is common) but fail with lighting changes (factory lights are different from lab lights). Papers address domain adaptation (learning to work across different environments by discovering what matters), adversarial attacks (handling deliberate disturbances by learning to ignore manipulation), and uncertainty quantification (knowing when the agent is confident and when it should ask for help rather than guess).

Safety is tied to reliability because one catastrophic failure (a robot dropping an expensive part, a vehicle crashing) undoes many good decisions and causes real harm. An agent that works well 99% of the time but fails catastrophically in edge cases is not safe enough for deployment because those rare failures will happen in real use, and the costs are not symmetric — one crash is worse than 99 good drives. Real-world deployment requires that the agent either handles surprises gracefully by adapting its behavior on the fly (when conditions shift, the agent continues working well because it adjusts), or recognizes when it encounters something completely new and asks a human for help rather than guessing and making the mistake worse. This is the same strategy humans use when facing uncertainty — some problems we solve, some we defer to someone with more expertise.

papers.title: An Orthogonal Learner for Individualized Outcomes in Markov Decision Processes
papers.contribution: A theoretically grounded meta-learner achieving doubly robust and quasi-oracle efficient Q-function estimation in both discrete and continuous state spaces.

papers.title: CSPO: Constraint-Sensitive Policy Optimization for Safe Reinforcement Learning
papers.contribution: Achieves faster safety recovery and high reward preservation on navigation and locomotion benchmarks, resulting in higher constrained returns than state-of-the-art methods.

papers.title: Clipped Q-Learning: Your Value Clipping Is Secretly A Robust Operator
papers.contribution: Polynomial regret guarantees with optimistic exploration; on control tasks shows robustness improvements consistent with theory; value clipping is a modular mechanism for general value-based RL.

papers.title: DR-SAC: Distributionally Robust Soft Actor-Critic for Reinforcement Learning under Uncertainty
papers.contribution: DR-SAC achieves up to 9.8x higher average reward than SAC baseline under common perturbations and significantly improves computational efficiency compared to existing DR-RL algorithms.

papers.title: Off-Policy Evaluation for Ranking Policies under Deterministic Logging Policies
papers.contribution: Our estimators achieve significantly lower bias than baselines, particularly under completely deterministic logging policies where existing methods incur substantial bias.

papers.title: Reward-Preserving Counterfactual State Editing for Offline Reinforcement Learning
papers.contribution: Experiments on D4RL locomotion, AntMaze, and offline recommendation benchmarks show consistent gains within the DT family, and CSET remains substantially more robust than strong value-based and DT baselines under injected spurious distractors..

papers.title: Robust Optimization for Mitigating Reward Hacking with Correlated Proxies
papers.contribution: Consistently outperforms ORPO in worst-case returns, offering improved robustness and stability across different proxy-true reward correlation levels.

papers.title: Safe Reinforcement Learning with Preference-based Constraint Inference
papers.contribution: Achieves superior alignment with true safety requirements and outperforms state-of-the-art baselines on safety and reward metrics.

papers.title: ASAP: Exploiting the Satisficing Generalization Edge in Neural Combinatorial Optimization
papers.contribution: Improves generalization on 3D-BPP, TSP, and CVRP with superior online adaptation; demonstrates that identifying promising actions is more generalizable than selecting optimal ones.

papers.title: Approximation of Log-Partition Function in Policy Mirror Descent Induces Implicit Regularization for LLM Post-Training
papers.contribution: Demonstrate PMD-mean improves stability and remains competitive in stale-rollout settings while enabling higher throughput through larger rollout batches.

papers.title: Breaking Multi-Task Curse: Reward-Weighted Evolution for Black-Box Many-Task Optimization
papers.contribution: Consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods on synthetic benchmarks, real-world engineering problems, and RL tasks, enabling skill transfer across morphologically distinct policies.

papers.title: Breaking Safety Paradox with Feasible Dual Policy Iteration
papers.contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art on Safety-Gymnasium with lowest violation and competitive-to-best return simultaneously.

papers.title: Budget-Efficient Attacks and Robustness Training for Cooperative MARL
papers.contribution: BHEA demonstrates stronger attacks under the same budget and substantially improves robustness to limited-step action hijacking on StarCraft Multi-Agent Challenge (SMAC) while reducing training overhead.

papers.title: Closing the Sim-to-Real Gap in Non-Markovian Spreading Processes via GPU-Accelerated Distributional RL
papers.contribution: Achieves 59× improvement over Markovian baselines and demonstrates robust zero-shot transfer to real-world social networks (Facebook, Twitter, YouTube).

papers.title: Constrained Meta Reinforcement Learning with Provable Test-Time Safety
papers.contribution: The method provides near-optimal policy learning on test tasks with provable safety, and derives a matching lower bound showing the sample complexity is tight.

papers.title: Corruption-Tolerant Asynchronous Q-Learning with Near-Optimal Rates
papers.contribution: Proves finite-time guarantees matching existing bounds plus an additive term scaling with the fraction of corrupted samples, with information-theoretic lower bounds showing near-optimality.

papers.title: Distributionally Robust Markov Games with Average Reward
papers.contribution: Provides comprehensive theoretical and algorithmic foundations for distributionally robust Markov games with average-reward criterion, including convergence proofs and approximation results from discounted to average-reward settings.

papers.title: From Absolute to Relative: Rethinking Reward Shaping in Group-Based Reinforcement Learning
papers.contribution: Consistent performance improvements over standard group-based baselines across reasoning and open-ended generation via relative reward framework.

papers.title: Geometric Control of Out-of-Distribution Shift in Safe Offline RL
papers.contribution: Achieves consistently low violation rates with competitive returns across multiple safe RL benchmarks through structured geometric regularization.

papers.title: Knothe-Rosenblatt Quantile Regression for Risk-sensitive Multi-objective Reinforcement Learning
papers.contribution: Risk-sensitive multi-objective RL framework with convergence guarantees under the distributional Bellman operator and improved performance on MO-Gymnasium benchmarks.

papers.title: Learning Generalizable Skill Policy with Data-Efficient Unsupervised RL
papers.contribution: GenDa significantly enhances scalability of URL with superior generality and sample efficiency for downstream task performance.

papers.title: Online Robust Reinforcement Learning with General Function Approximation
papers.contribution: First regret guarantee for online DR-RL with general function approximation, achieving sublinear regret independent of state and action space size.

papers.title: Optimal Robust Subsidy Policies for Irrational Agent in Principal-Agent MDPs
papers.contribution: Shows optimal subsidies concentrate along social-welfare-maximizing trajectories and characterizes welfare loss under bounded rationality.

papers.title: R2R2: Robust Representation for Intensive Experience Reuse via Redundancy Reduction in Self-Predictive Learning
papers.contribution: At UTD ratio of 20, improves TD7 by ~22% and provides additional gains on SimbaV2-SPL.

papers.title: REG: In-Sample RL via Regularizing the Evaluation Gap
papers.contribution: Matches state-of-the-art performance among Gaussian and diffusion-based methods without the computational burden of diffusion approaches.

papers.title: Rationality Measurement and Theory for Reinforcement Learning Agents
papers.contribution: Bounds risk gap by Wasserstein distance between distributions and empirical Rademacher complexity; theory supports benefits of regularizers and domain randomization.

papers.title: Robust Adaptive Multi-Step Predictive Shielding
papers.contribution: Significantly reduces safety violations compared to existing safe RL methods while maintaining high task performance in complex control environments.

papers.title: Robust In-Context Reinforcement Learning Under Reward Poisoning Attacks
papers.contribution: Significantly outperforms robust baselines in bandit settings under learned attackers and generalizes to complex environments including adaptive attackers and MDPs.

papers.title: Robustness in the Face of Partial Identifiability in Reward Learning
papers.contribution: Rob-ReL addresses identifiability problems in policy preference assessment with convergence and generalization analyses elucidating performance impacts while ensuring controlled acceleration.

papers.title: SMAC: Score-Matched Actor-Critics for Robust Offline-to-Online Transfer
papers.contribution: In 4/6 environments, it reduces regret by 34-58% over the best baseline

papers.title: Safe In-Context Reinforcement Learning
papers.contribution: Consistently enables safe and robust in-context adaptation across challenging benchmarks, outperforming existing ICRL and safe meta-RL baselines.

papers.title: Safety Generalization Under Distribution Shift in Safe Reinforcement Learning: A Diabetes Testbed
papers.contribution: Test-time shielding achieves 13-14% Time-in-Range gains across algorithms and patient populations while reducing clinical risk index and glucose variability.

papers.title: Self-Improving Skill Learning for Robust Skill-based Meta-Reinforcement Learning
papers.contribution: Achieves robust and stable adaptation under noisy and suboptimal data, consistently outperforming other skill-based meta-RL methods on diverse long-horizon tasks.

papers.title: Solving Parameter-Robust Avoid Problems with Unknown Feasibility using Reinforcement Learning
papers.contribution: FGE learns policies with over 50% more coverage than existing methods on challenging MuJoCo and Kinetix tasks with pixel observations.

papers.title: TraCeS: Learning Per-Timestep Constraint-Violation Credit from Sparse Trajectory-Level Labels
papers.contribution: Improves constraint satisfaction and feedback efficiency over baselines across continuous-control benchmarks, including long-horizon and noisy-label settings.

papers.title: Transferable Reinforcement Learning via Probabilistic Latent Embeddings and Dynamic Policy Adaptation for Sim-to-Real Deployment
papers.contribution: Enables safe and efficient policy transfer via latent context inference and dynamic risk adjustment, addressing unmodeled system dynamics.

papers.title: Unraveling the Complexity of Memory in RL Agents: an Approach for Classification and Evaluation
papers.contribution: Standardized framework and methodology enable objective evaluation and categorization of different memory classes in RL agents.
